questions.question_text: A reducing balance loan of $\$7500$ is charged interest at $14.4\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, with monthly repayments of $\$400$. What is the balance owing at the end of the first month?

options.why: Subtracted the repayment but forgot to add the month's interest.
Subtracted the interest instead of adding it to the opening balance.
Used the annual rate $14.4\%$ for one month instead of dividing it by $12$.

questions.question_text: A reducing balance loan of $\$20\,000$ is charged interest at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, with monthly repayments of $\$650$. What is the balance owing at the end of the second month?

options.why: Stopped after the first month instead of going on to the second.
Subtracted two repayments and ignored the interest charged each month.
Charged the second month's interest on the original $\$20\,000$ rather than on the reduced balance.

questions.question_text: In one month of a reducing balance loan the opening balance is $\$84\,200$ and the interest charged is $\$547.30$. What is the monthly interest rate, as a percentage?

options.why: Gave the annual rate $0.65\% \times 12$ rather than the monthly rate asked for.
Moved the decimal point one place too few when converting $0.0065$ to a percentage.
Moved the decimal point one place too many when converting $0.0065$ to a percentage.

questions.question_text: A reducing balance loan of $\$145\,000$ is repaid by monthly repayments of $\$1120$ over $20$ years. What is the total interest charged?

options.why: Gave the total amount repaid instead of subtracting the amount borrowed.
Used a $25$-year term ($300$ repayments) instead of $20$ years.
Gave the amount borrowed rather than the interest charged.

questions.solution_text:
Number of repayments $= 20 \times 12 = 240$

Total repaid $= 1120 \times 240$
$= \$268\,800$

Total interest $= 268\,800 - 145\,000$
$= \$123\,800$

questions.question_text: A reducing balance loan of $\$16\,000$ is charged interest at $9.6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, with monthly repayments of $\$550$. Of the amount repaid in the first two months, how much was interest? Round each month's interest to the nearest cent.

options.why: Charged the same $\$128$ in both months instead of using the reduced balance in month $2$.
Gave the first month's interest only rather than the total over two months.
Gave the total repaid over two months instead of the interest part of it.
Assumed the balance falls at a steady rate, leaving one third after two thirds of the term.
Read the balance at $60$ months instead of at $120$ months.
Read the balance at $150$ months instead of at $120$ months.

questions.solution_text:
Find $120$ on the horizontal axis and read up to the curve.
The curve is level with the $\$60\,000$ gridline there.
About $\$60\,000$ is still owing after $120$ months.

questions.question_text: Owen owes $\$3800$ on a reducing balance loan charged at $22.8\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, and he repays $\$70$ each month. Which statement about his loan is correct?

options.text: The monthly interest of $\$72.20$ is more than the repayment, so the balance grows and the loan is never repaid.
The monthly interest of $\$72.20$ is more than the repayment, but the balance still falls slowly.
options.why: Adding $\$72.20$ and taking off $\$70$ increases the balance; it cannot fall.

options.text: The monthly interest is $\$6.02$, so the balance falls by about $\$64$ each month.
options.why: Divided the annual rate by $12$ twice, giving a rate of $0.158\%$ instead of $1.9\%$.

options.text: The monthly interest is $\$866.40$, so the balance grows by almost $\$800$ each month.
options.why: Used the annual rate $22.8\%$ as if it were the monthly rate.

questions.solution_text:
Rate per month $= \dfrac{0.228}{12} = 0.019$

$I = 3800 \times 0.019$
$= \$72.20$

Since $\$72.20 > \$70$, the balance rises each month and the loan is never repaid.

questions.question_text: A reducing balance loan of $\$25\,000$ is charged interest at $10.8\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, with monthly repayments of $\$1200$. What is the balance owing at the end of the third month? Round each month's interest to the nearest cent.

options.why: Subtracted three repayments and ignored the interest charged each month.
Stopped at the end of the second month instead of the third.
Charged $\$225$ of interest every month instead of recalculating it on the falling balance.
